en: The last extension I personally like having
is the Subagents extension,
Pi Subagents, also by Nico Priem, the same
person who created that Web Access
extension.
And Subagents allows Pi to create and spin
up subagents in its main session so that it
can offload certain work like research work
to subagents which have their own fresh
context window and don't pollute the main
context window
and can then report back to the main agent
once they're done. This is a feature many
coding agents like Claude Code have built
in. Pi does not, but because it's so
extensible, there are packages like this
which add this feature. And it is a feature
I personally like having. So it is another
extension I installed. That's the command
for installing it.
Py install npm
py-subagents.
With that, it is available.
And if you then start Pi,
you can
run /subagents doctor to show some
diagnostics.
And this also should show you
how many subagents are available because
just installing this extension already sets
up some subagents. But you can then also, as
always, dive into the official docs of this
package to configure it in greater detail.
Again, not something you have to do, not
something I did. I'm fine with the built-in
subagents you have, which are already
prepared for the most common tasks like
exploring the file system or doing
researching, but you can tweak everything to
your liking if you want to.
You can use the regular Pi settings file for
overriding package-specific settings, for
this subagents package. And you can also use
the local settings file instead if you have
project-specific overrides or changes. If
you run
/subagents/models,
you see which AI models will be used for the
different subagents.
And you can also easily tweak them, as
you'll see in the next lecture.
